alignment.note: the reproduction is this far from where the original has the same floor

P1.reason: Some of the arrangement is there: a long north-south central corridor splits the map into a west half and an east half, and there is an annex with stairs on the east side. The rest is off. In the original each half is an octagonal ring with chamfered diagonal corridors around an inner room, and a hexagonal hall sits on each side of the central corridor. The reproduction has two rectangular blocks of square rooms with a cross-shaped hub in the middle. The diagonal corner corridors, the hex halls and the ring loops that join the areas are all missing.

P2.reason: The measured floor overlap is 0.375, far below the 0.70 needed. The overall extent is close (2456x2062 against 2432x2080), but inside it the areas are in different places and have different shapes. The original's octagonal outline and its open hex halls become full rectangles in the reproduction, and the east annex is a different shape and size.

P3.reason: The reproduction has the floors at 0, 160 and 320 but not the original's z 512 upper ledges on either side of the centre. The section shows the original's stepped balconies at 160/320/512 under a tall split ceiling. The reproduction has thin 320 slabs, a different ceiling profile with sloped sides and a tower, and an extra low room at the far west.

P4.reason: Only 34.5% of entities are matched, against the 80% required. The entity counts are equal (58) and the classes are broadly the same, but most of them are misplaced: deathmatch starts at -552 -632 224 and 608 496 224, the 9mmAR clusters at -384 0 176 and 608 448 16, the gauss clips, the batteries, the z 336 ledge items (grenades, ARgrenades, buckshot).

P5.reason: The original uses dark blue-grey concrete walls with recessed computer-bank windows and a brown tiled floor with a yellow kick strip. The reproduction uses pale mottled concrete, metal grate floors and a different blue-grey computer-panel strip with yellow trim. A player would notice the difference at once in every view.

P6.reason: The original is dim, and several of its starts (5, 6, 7) are nearly black. The reproduction is evenly bright everywhere, with a dense grid of lights. Starts 1 to 4 are also much brighter and flatter than the original. The bright and dark areas do not match.

P7.reason: The central corridor and some square pillars are present. Missing: the original's window-like computer-bank recesses along the walls, the chamfered octagonal corridors, the hex halls, and the ceiling light fixture and tile floor of the corridor (start 8). Generic panel strips and grates stand in for them.

P8.reason: There are no check errors and the walk test leaves 0 places unreached in the reproduction, so every start reaches every weapon and item on foot.

P9.reason: Views 1 to 7 show plain pale concrete boxes, grates or bright panel walls where the original has dark computer-bank recesses or near-darkness. Only start 8 (a long corridor) is broadly similar in shape, and its textures and lighting differ. A player who knows the map would not recognise it.
